Commentary.Commentary: Welcome back for England's reply. The two umpires and the Sri Lankan players have made their way out to the middle.  Ben Duckett and Dan Lawrence stride out to open their innings. Vishwa Fernando will kickstart proceedings with the new ball for Sri Lanka. Away we go...
... FOURTH INNINGS ....

For England, Chris Woakes and Atkinson were lethal early on, while Matthew Potts stepped up effectively in Mark Wood's absence earlier in the day. Despite minimal assistance from the pitch, the pacers did well to restrain the Sri Lankan innings, maintaining their composure even as partnerships began to form. Woakes and Potts shared 3 wickets apiece while Atkinson snared 2. What was impressive was the way England came back post the first session. They were looking jaded once Wood was out of the attack but a good lunch has helped them. They need 205 runs to win and take the lead in the series. While time is on their side, they'll have to be cautious with a long tail waiting in the wings. As for Sri Lanka, they will have to make the new ball count and put England under pressure with early wickets. Stay tuned for the second essay.

Wow. That escalated quickly. Sri Lanka were looking at a lead of somewhere around 250 at Lunch, but Kamindu Mendis' wicket set the cat scurrying amongst the pigeons. But overall, given that they were 1 for 2 on Friday, this has been a good fight from the visitors. The top order was blown apart but the experience of Karunaratne, Mathews and Chandimal came to the fore. Not to forget, Chandimal was injured as well, visiting the hospital and in danger of being ruled out of the match. But he came back this morning and anchored the innings, with excellent support from Kamindu Mendis. This morning, Mathews did mention to the broadcasters that they would be targeting somewhere around 200 to chase for the hosts - the bowlers have got something to defend, at least.

Commentary.Commentary: Welcome back for the start of the second session on Day 4. The sun is shining in all its glory as the two umpires and players make their way out to the middle. Dinesh Chandimal marks his guard and gets ready to face Chris Woakes first up after Lunch. Here we go!
... DAY 4, SESSION 2 ...

With a lead of 169 runs, Sri Lanka will not want to think too far ahead. They will be focused on starting well after Lunch and then take it from there. England, on the other hand, have a lot of work to do and will need to make the most of the new ball, which is just 2 overs old, when play resumes after Lunch. Join us back at 12.55 pm GMT for what promises to be another enthralling session of Test cricket.

On the other hand, England have been left scratching their heads, struggling to find a way to break this partnership. The absence of Mark Wood, sidelined for the day due to a right thigh muscle injury, was clearly felt as the hosts lacked the penetrative edge needed to create consistent pressure. The lack of help from the surface made the job even more challenging for the pacers as well as Shoaib Bashir.

Sri Lanka take the honours of the morning session on Day 4! The visitors dominated the session, adding 87 runs from 22 overs without losing a wicket. Starting the day with an 82-run lead, Sri Lanka made an encouraging start. Both Kamindu Mendis and Dinesh Chandimal batted with intent, capitalizing on loose deliveries and keeping the scoreboard ticking. The surface seemed to have slowed down, offering no major alarms as both went about their business nicely. Even the brief rain interruption could not dislodge them as Mendis brought up his third Test ton before Lunch.

JUST IN - England have been dealt a blow ahead of the start of play as Mark Wood will not take the field on Day 4 due to a right thigh muscle injury. Wood, who walked off the field late yesterday, will continue to be assessed by the England medical team.

Mathews couldn’t capitalise on his lifeline, but Mendis continued to battle, keeping Sri Lanka’s hopes alive. Having returned with a clear X-ray, Chandimal came back to the crease and, along with Mendis, guided Sri Lanka through to the close of play with a lead of 82 runs. Today, the visitors face two key challenges - first, surviving the crucial first hour, and then handling the second new ball, which is 20 overs away. England, on the other hand, will be eager to dismiss these two set batters and get a crack at the tail with the new red cherry. Stick around as the first ball on Day 4 is not far away.

However, Angelo Mathews and Kamindu Mendis showed immense grit, digging deep to erase the deficit and even push Sri Lanka into the lead. But as we’ve seen so often during this and the previous English summer, the replacement ball did a lot more than the previous one, and yesterday was no exception. However, the English fielders couldn’t fully back up their bowlers, giving reprieves to both Mathews and Mendis.

Jamie Smith’s maiden Test century was the standout performance for England, guiding them to a solid first-innings lead of 122 runs. In response, Sri Lanka were rocked early and suffered further setbacks as the English pacers chipped away at the wickets. The situation looked bleak for the visitors when Dinesh Chandimal had to walk off after taking a blow to his right thumb.

Hello and a warm welcome, folks! Day 4 is upon us, and it could very well be the final day of this intriguing first Test. After three days of gripping action, England have their noses in front and will be confident of wrapping things up today. As for Sri Lanka, they aren’t completely out of the contest, but it will take a monumental effort to turn the tide in their favour.

The final hour of play saw England's bowlers struggle to maintain pressure. Milan Ratnayake then joined in and got off to a decent start. It felt like he could be able to repeat the heroics of the first innings, but it wasn't the case as Joe Root was forced to step up to fill the void, making an immediate impact by claiming his wicket on his second delivery. Yet, Mendis held firm, ensuring Sri Lanka reached stumps without further damage and with a lead of 82 runs. It was a captivating end to a day filled with ups and downs. England need early wickets at the start of Day 4 or this 82 can turn into a daunting total. England will be targeting Angelo Mathews as a key wicket after the break, aiming to dismantle the remaining Sri Lankan batting lineup and make significant inroads. Meanwhile, Sri Lanka will be focused on overcoming the 15-run deficit and building a robust total. Another thrilling session of play is undoubtedly on the horizon. After a shaky start, Angelo Mathews has bounced back strongly and is now standing tall against the odds, having scored 48 unbeaten runs. Not only has he been effectively contributing to the scoreboard, but he has also been a guiding force, motivating his partners to provide the solid support he needs, which has been lacking so far.

However, Mark Wood made an immediate impact upon entering the attack, ending the resilient partnership between Karunaratne and Mathews. Pope and Co. pressed hard for consecutive wickets, but Angelo Mathews and Dinesh Chandimal steadied the innings, restoring some composure to the Sri Lankan side. Just as things were looking up for Sri Lanka, Dinesh Chandimal received a painful blow to his right thumb and was forced to retire hurt. Following this setback, skipper Dhananjaya de Silva, who had hoped to replicate his first innings performance, struggled and the situation began to deteriorate a bit.

TEA, DAY 2 - Session Summary -  27 overs, 97 runs, and 2 wickets. Despite Sri Lanka losing two more wickets in this session, they have managed to find some stability after a rocky start. Dimuth Karunaratne and the experienced Angelo Mathews steadied the ship with a crucial partnership, adding 51 runs off 69 deliveries.

Chris Woakes bowls a good-length delivery on middle, angling it away but shapes it back in on the middle. Dimuth Karunaratne hangs back and looks to push it away but gets squared up and the ball attacks the middle and it thumps his upper pad. The review shows that there's no bat involved in UltraEdge and the Ball Tracking shows that the ball misses the top of the middle stump because of the bounce. The decision remains the same and England lose a review!

Commentary.Commentary: We are back with the afternoon session of this 'Moving Day'! The umpires are out in the middle and England are in a tight-knit huddle alongside the ropes before they spread out to take the field. Dimuth Karunaratne and Angelo Mathews stride out set to resume their stay at the crease. Looks like, Ollie Pope has decided to start with spin and has tossed the ball to Shoaib Bashir who will begin the proceedings for England. Here we go..
... DAY 3, SESSION 2 ...

With momentum firmly on their side, the English duo of Chris Woakes and Gus Atkinson returned with intent, delivering hard lengths that resulted in the dismissals of Nishan Madushka and Kusal Mendis in successive overs, further tilting the game in England's favour. Sri Lanka's top order once again failed to navigate the challenging early phase, as they had in the first innings. With a break in play, the visitors will need to regroup and approach the next session with caution and strategy. England, on the other hand, will be eager to continue their dominance and push for a decisive result. An intriguing second session of play awaits. Join us in about 40 minutes for the start of the action.

Prabath Jayasuriya then broke through, dismissing Smith for 111, a crucial wicket that alleviated much of the pressure on the visitors. Once the second new ball was introduced, Mark Wood exploited its hardness, contributing a quickfire cameo of 22 off just 13 balls before being bowled by Asitha Fernando. Vishwa Fernando then wrapped up the innings, taking the final wicket.

Early in the day, Sri Lanka appeared unsettled from the outset, struggling with inconsistent line and length, which allowed Jamie Smith and Gus Atkinson to comfortably resume their established partnership from the previous evening. Both batters capitalized on the first hour of play, steadily accumulating runs with ease. Jamie Smith reached a significant milestone, notching his maiden Test century, but soon after, Atkinson was dismissed by Milan Rathnayake, who claimed his first Test wicket.

Wow, what an eventful session we've witnessed! A total of 27.3 overs, 109 Runs and 6 Wickets. After a strong batting performance that secured a 122-run lead, England have carried that momentum into their bowling. They've made an ideal start, picking up two big wickets in just 3 overs while conceding only 10 runs heading into Lunch on Day 3.
